01.r: A cry of threatened doom over the builder.
01.n: Gesenius gives this word three uses: threatening ('woe!'), lamenting ('alas!') and admonishing ('ho!'). Here it is the first.

02.r: The man at work raising his house, the king of the verses around it.
02.n: A participle: someone in the act of building. That this is aimed at a king of Judah is a reasonable reading from the palace and its upper rooms; the verse itself names no one.

03.r: His dwelling, here a grand one.
03.n: The ordinary word for house; the BSB says 'palace'.

04.r: Built with no righteousness in it.
04.n: Literally 'with not': the preposition joined to the word 'not' makes 'without'. Most translations fold the 'not' into 'unrighteousness'.

05.r: What is right in the way he deals with people.
05.n: Gesenius: in a physical sense straightness, and so rectitude, what is right and just. The brief's lexicon lists 'righteousness in government' among its senses.

06.r: The rooms on top, added to his house.
06.n: Gesenius: an upper chamber, a loft on the roof of a house.

08.r: Fair judgment, what a ruler owes his people.
08.n: Gesenius gives first 'judgment', the act of judging; BDB adds 'justice, right'. Paired with 'righteousness' just before it, as often in the Hebrew Bible.

09.r: A fellow member of his own people.
09.n: The brief's lexicon: friend, companion, and in a weaker sense fellow citizen, another person. The Hebrew says 'by his neighbour' or 'with his neighbour': the work is done by means of the neighbour.

10.r: He makes his neighbour labour for him.
10.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as to labour, to work, and the brief's lexicon lists 'to work for another, serve another by labour'. With 'by his neighbour' it means he gets his work done through the other man. Our 'who' is English glue; the Hebrew simply goes on with a new verb.

11.n: Gesenius: gratis, gratuitously, for nothing, and also 'in vain' and 'without cause'. The DRC takes the last sense, 'without cause'.

12.n: The word's first sense is a deed or work; the brief's lexicon lists 'wages of work' among its senses, and Gesenius notes this verse for the spelling. The KJV and Geneva keep 'his work'.

14.r: He does not pay what is owed.
14.n: STEPBible tags this occurrence with the sense 'pay'.

15.r: The neighbour who did the work.

02.n: The Greek has no 'woe': it opens 'The one building his house'.

11.n: δωρεάν, 'as a gift', freely: the word Gesenius sets beside this Hebrew one.

12.n: μισθός, wage, the word our register renders 'wage(s)' in the New Testament.

13.n: οὐ μὴ, a strong double negative: 'he will by no means give back'.

14.n: ἀποδίδωμι, to give back, render what is owed.
